description: The Fighting Illini smashed records in a 120-45 rout of Fairleigh Dickinson
body:
The Fighting Illini smashed records in a 120-45 rout of Fairleigh Dickinson
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    10:38 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        College basketball's much-needed return on opening night is Christmas Day … until it starts to get hairy in the second half of a buy game. Just ask North Carolina's Michael Malone, who had to bench his starters midway through the middle of a second-half collapse against Western Carolina. UNC, with help from an untimely technical on the Catamounts, avoided disaster in Monday's 80-72 win, but it was a pucker-worthy showing from a $20 million roster that looks far from the top of the ACC pecking order.The Field of 68 also garners some well-deserved recognition for bringing back the opening day marathon! Grambling State and Northern Illinois played one of Monday's best games in a 4 a.m. banger. The Tigers of Grambling State won 89-87.Let's dive into the rest of the winners and losers from Monday's slate.Winner: Illinois is good at the whole offense thingThe Illini are in the middle of changing their offensive gameplan, pivoting from a team that played slow and relied heavily on pick-and-rolls into a zoom-zoom transition attack that basically has no plays.It took one game to break record books.The 75-point margin of victory was the largest for Illinois at the State Farm Center, which opened in 1963. The Illini fell seven points short of tying the school record for points in a game.  
The Illini drained a program-best 19 3-pointers in a 120-45 romp over FDU. They shot 51 3-pointers. They went 26-for-31 on layups or dunks. 30 of the 46 buckets were assisted. These stat lines were bonkers:Andrej Stojakovic: 20 points, seven rebounds, four assists.Quentin Coleman: 13 points, 10 rebounds, six assists.Ethan Brown: 12 points, nine rebounds, seven assists.Stefan Vaaks: 20 points, four assists, zero turnovers.Seven different players deposited multiple treys. Offensive coordinator Tyler Underwood remains at the top of his craft, and Brad Underwood's willingness to change may be his strongest attribute. Even stronger than excellent evals of guys like Brown, who was a three-star recruit with no high-major offers and all of a sudden looks every bit the part of a multi-year Big Ten starter.Illinois' performance was even more impressive considering the Illini were playing without CBS Sports First Team All-American David Mirkovic, who is recovering from early August foot surgery and underwent an appendectomy Saturday and is out indefinitely.  – Isaac Trotter
Winner: Thomas Haugh shows why he's a top NPOTY contenderThomas Haugh has two games with four 3-pointers made in his Florida career: In the Elite Eight against Texas Tech in 2025 and on Monday against Miami. Haugh shot a respectable 32.6% on 5.9 attempts from beyond the arc last season, but one of the best shooting nights of his career came in the first game of the new season.And it wasn't just the shooting that stood out. Haugh, known as the ultimate Swiss Army Knife, finished with 10 rebounds, four assists and a block and a steal to go along with his 19 points. Michigan State guard Jeremy Fears Jr. was CBS Sports Preseason Player of the Year. However, there is a case for Haugh winning the award. And if this was any indication, it's going to be a special season for Haugh and the Gators. – Cameron Salerno
        
            
                No. 1 Florida opens season with convincing victory vs. Miami: Gators show why they deserve No. 1 ranking
                
                    Cameron Salerno                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Loser: Malik Reneau's struggles against elite competition continueReneau led Miami in scoring last year at nearly 18 points per game. It was a big boon to get him back for a fifth year of eligibility, but he had no real answer for Florida's elite frontcourt. Reneau fouled out in 24 minutes and finished with just five points, including an 0-for-5 mark on 2-pointers. Reneau is now shooting just 50% on 2-pointers in his last 25 games against top-50 opponents. Miami will have to get through elite teams if it wants to make the Final Four. It needs more from Reneau to scale that mountain. – Trotter
Loser: Iowa State isn't the same ole Iowa State yetMemphis knocked off No. 18 Iowa State 80-76, behind 26 points from Jayden Reid and an 18-point, eight-rebound showing from SEMO transfer Luke Almodovar. Iowa State entered Monday rated No. 6 on KenPom.com. That seemed high for a roster that lost Milan Momcilovic (to Kentucky) and Joshua Jefferson (to the NBA). The first impression hints that Iowa State isn't close to a top-10 team at the moment. Not without injured defensive maven Killyan Toure. Not if breakout candidate Jamarion Batemon is going to go scoreless. Not if Tamin Lipsey is going to score just 12 points on 13 shots, while looking pretty rusty. T.J. Otzelberger's group has a ton of work to do. – TrotterWinner and loser: UCF does UCF stuff while Dior Johnson does Dior Johnson stuffDior Johnson scored 41 points, as Dior Johnson is one to do. Meanwhile, UCF survived FGCU 96-95 in overtime. I don't have high hopes for UCF in the Big 12 this year, but at least Johnson is going to go absolutely insane like once a week. – Trotter
Winner: This is only the beginning for High PointHigh Point coach Flynn Clayman, clad in his ice-cold purple suit, was back in the spotlight, and his Panthers delivered a 72-57 shellacking of a good Liberty squad. High Point's point-of-attack defense is going to be a major strength this season. South Florida transfer CJ Brown and top-150 freshman Trey Pearson are hounding defenders who were draped onto Liberty's point guards for all 40 minutes. 
This High Point squad does not project to be an awesome 3-point shooting team, but its best offense could be this suffocating defense that can lead to numerous good looks in the open floor. Pearson and ex-Arizona walk-on Conrad Martinez combined for 21 points, seven rebounds, three assists and just one turnover. Oh, and they both were coming off the bench. Clayman's got another real-deal squad. High Point is currently favored by double figures in every single Big South game. – TrotterWinner: This is only the beginning for Murray State, tooMurray State has some of the deepest pockets at the mid-major ranks, and this roster looks like a high-major outfit. Full stop. The Racers buried Tennessee State 94-64, with a new defensive recipe. Murray State has flipped from a passive to an aggressive defensive scheme, and it passed the first test with flying colors. Tennessee State, filled with numerous former high-major names like Arterio Morris (Texas), Aaron Bradshaw (Kentucky) and Ty-Laur Johnson (Wake Forest), turned the basketball over a whopping 26 times. Murray State was everywhere. Sophomore wing Roman Domon was awesome, finishing with 22 points, five rebounds, two assists, a block and a steal. Domon has a chance to get paid to play basketball for a very long time. This team is deep and talented, but it also has so much room to grow. If the first impression is any indication, Murray State has the pieces to earn an at-large bid. That hasn't happened for the Missouri Valley since 2021. – Trotter

title: Michael Malone's debut as North Carolina coach exposes issues in Tar Heels' ugly win vs. Western Carolina - CBS Sports
description: The Tar Heels were bullied on the offensive glass and needed a late swing to survive an alarming opening test und
body:
The Tar Heels were bullied on the offensive glass and needed a late swing to survive an alarming opening test under their new coach
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    11:17 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        A band of Catamounts nearly derailed Michael Malone's honeymoon with North Carolina on Monday night. Though UNC avoided a disastrous loss, its 80-72 win over Western Carolina came layered in red flags.The Catamounts gave UNC everything it could handle, cutting the Tar Heels' lead to one twice in the second half. It wasn't until Western Carolina's lead guard, Jaeden Roberts, fouled out with 5:57 remaining that UNC gained a bit of breathing room.Moments later, a questionable over-the-back call on Western Carolina wiped off a putback and begat a technical foul on the Catamounts. By the time North Carolina was done shooting free throws, the sequence had produced a 6-point swing at the 5:25 mark, extending UNC's lead to 69-62. Without Roberts on the floor, Western Carolina couldn't climb all the way back as Malone's squad avoided catastrophe.On a night when other unranked high-major teams with first-year coaches like NC State, Syracuse and Providence all cruised to easy wins in buy games, North Carolina's ugly slog made it an outlier.

        
            
                College basketball scores, opening night winners and losers: No. 3 Illinois rolls, Memphis shocks Iowa State
                
                    Isaac Trotter                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Catamounts give Tar Heels a scare  After entering as 22-point underdogs, the Catamounts — picked to finish eighth in the SoCon — looked like nearly an even match for UNC in Malone's coaching debut.
North Carolina jumped out to a 10-0 lead behind eight straight points from NC State transfer Matt Able. It looked like the Tar Heels might be off to the races, like in the only prior meeting between the in-state foes. UNC won that game 104-61 in December 2017. That's what this game should have been for the Tar Heels. It should have been an easy start that engendered optimism for the start of a new regime.
Instead, it underscored fears that arose during North Carolina's 2-1 exhibition slate, which included an uncomfortable overtime win over Charlotte. North Carolina's shortcomings exposedUNC was outworked 12-6 on the offensive glass vs. Charlotte in the exhibition game, resulting in an 18-10 edge in second-chance points for the 49ers.Western Carolina followed a similar blueprint, using a 13-7 advantage in offensive rebounds to create a 13-8 advantage in second-chance points.
Starting center Sayon Keita has a 7-foot-7 wingspan, but it's clear the lanky 18 year old doesn't know how to use it yet. Keita and starting power forward Jarin Stevenson finished with just four rebounds apiece."You do all that hard work, only to see the shot taken and now they get an extra opportunity," Malone said. "I think it's something where we just have to continue to harp on it, drill it, demand it. I'm going to keep on pounding that rock. It's going to break one day."Veesaar leaves void for HeelsThat Malone and UNC couldn't retain 7-footer Henri Veesaar, who left to be the No. 52 pick in the NBA Draft, is going to haunt the Tar Heels.
UNC still had time after Veesaar's departure to find a suitable replacement. The Tar Heels didn't do it.An opponent with more competent bigs than Western Carolina will make life miserable for this UNC team unless the Tar Heels resolve soon to make crashing the boards a higher priority. Indiana certainly did in a 76-58 exhibition win over the Tar Heels. The Hoosiers used a 20-10 edge in offensive rebounds to create a 17-7 edge in second-chance points. At the time, it could be written off as an exhibition aberration. Now, it's a verified problem."One thing I do know is that both Jarin Stevenson and Sayon Keita, it's not like they're not playing hard," Malone said. "It's not like they're out there not giving effort. So we'll watch some film, see what's really causing it. But big picture, yes, we need Jarin and Sayon to be 7-10 boards every night."
ACC foes will feastLooking ahead to ACC play, what is Louisville center Flory Bidunga going to do against this team? What about hulking Florida State freshman Marcis Ponder? Most importantly, there are two games with Duke coming. The Blue Devils might have the most imposing front court in college basketball between junior center Patrick Ngongba and freshman phenom Joaquim Boumtje-Boumtje.The version of North Carolina's front court on display against Western Carolina will get demolished against those teams unless something changes quickly.If this were the NBA world that Malone came from, his front office could go to the free agency scrap heap and sign the meanest big man available. Or, the Tar Heels could make a trade to address their deficiencies. 
But roster construction season is over, and Malone's UNC honeymoon will be over soon, too, unless the Tar Heels can cultivate some rapid development in their frontcourt.

title: Florida opens season with convincing victory vs. Miami: Gators show why they deserve their No. 1 ranking - CBS Sports
description: Top-ranked Florida returned to where its season came to an end in March and easily handled the No. 14 Hurricanes
body:
Top-ranked Florida returned to where its season came to an end in March and easily handled the No. 14 Hurricanes
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    9:00 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        TAMPA, Fla. --  No. 1 Florida opened the 2026-27 college basketball season with a statement Monday, defeating No. 14 Miami 77-67 behind a huge night from national player of the year candidate Thomas Haugh. The star forward who bypassed the NBA Draft to return for his senior season with the Gators finished with a team-high 19 points and 10 rebounds.Haugh matched the best 3-point shooting night of his college career against Miami by draining four of his eight shots from beyond the arc. The last time Haugh knocked down four 3-pointers in a game came against Texas Tech in the 2025 Elite Eight. Florida went on to win the national title that year, and the Gators look like this season could produce a similar run.Seven months ago, Florida lost to Iowa here at Benchmark International Arena in the second round of the NCAA Tournament in one of the most shocking results of the entire season. Haugh, Rueben Chinyelu, Alex Condon, Boogie Fland and Urban Klavžar returned from that team that lost in this arena.Florida (1-0) also brought back Denzel Aberdeen — who was on Florida's national title team in 2025 before transferring to Kentucky and then back to Florida this offseason. Aberdeen is one of many players who were granted a fifth year of eligibility to play this season.
Chinyelu and the rest of this Florida team entered the season with confidence, as shown in an interview with CBS Sports' Matt Norlander before the season began. When asked to fill in the blank on what it would take for the Gators to win their second national title in three seasons, Chinyelu said there would be no "what if" and that his team was "winning it."Cocksure confidence? Maybe. But if the Gators play as they did against a very good Miami team, a second title in three seasons won't be out of the question. Let's dive into the biggest takeaways.Haugh's POTY campaign beginsHaugh has two games with four 3-pointers made in his Florida career: In the Elite Eight against Texas Tech in 2025 and on Monday vs. Miami. Haugh shot a respectable 32.6% on 5.9 attempts from beyond the arc last season, but the best shooting night of his career came in the first game of the new season.
And it wasn't just the shooting that stood out. Haugh, known as the ultimate Swiss Army Knife, did a little bit of everything in the win over the Hurricanes. Michigan State guard Jeremy Fears Jr. was CBS Sports Preseason Player of the Year. However, there is a case for Haugh winning the award. And if this was any indication, it's going to be a special season for Haugh and the Gators.
Miami will learn from this gameIt's no hyperbole to say that, aside from maybe facing ACC rival Duke, this was the toughest team Miami could've opened against. There's no shame in losing to the top-ranked Gators because this might just be the team to beat in the sport. There are some similarities between Florida and Miami because both are built around strong frontcourt play. The Hurricanes' nonconference schedule gets significantly more favorable after this game, but there will still be tests before ACC play begins. Miami faces Alabama and Texas before facing NC State in its ACC opener right before New Year's Eve. Miami should have a big season under Jai Lucas. A loss like this could be beneficial come March. And maybe, just maybe, a rematch could be in store around that time of year.
Florida's frontline is going to give opponents nightmaresIf you didn't already know, Florida's frontline is the best in the country. The trio of Haugh, Chinyelu and Condon are so physical on both ends of the floor that it wears opponents out as the game goes on. Even against a stout Miami frontcourt that elected to go big against the Gators with Henderson/Caleb Gaskins/Malik Reneau, it didn't matter.When that trio is on the floor together, they're extremely impactful by creating second-chance points on offense and disrupting the lane on the defensive end. Florida has the luxury of subbing in one of those players and going "small," with Klavžar coming off the bench. Florida is going to be a very, very tough out.Acaden Lewis looks like Miami's best playerThe biggest takeaway on the Miami front was how good Lewis looked. He finished with a game-high 24 points and looked in control while running the offense. The Villanova transfer had a strong freshman season but looks poised to take a massive jump in Year 2 in Jai Lucas' system. His shotmaking is very impressive for a guard and it wouldn't be a surprise at all to see him finish the year as the leading scorer for the Canes.

title: What's next for the Dream and Angel Reese? Why Atlanta should be right back in contention - CBS Sports
description: The Dream fell short once again in the WNBA Finals, but they'll bring back key contributors in 2027
body:
The Dream fell short once again in the WNBA Finals, but they'll bring back key contributors in 2027
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:07 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            7 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The first three times the Atlanta Dream made the WNBA Finals, they were swept. Their trip this season was even more heartbreaking. They led the 2026 WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries 2-1, and the Dream led Game 7 by nine in the second half falling short to Gabby Williams and the second-year franchise on Saturday night.The Dream's four losses in the Finals are tied for the second-most in WNBA history, and the Connecticut Sun is the only other franchise to make the Finals at least four times without winning a championship. Now that the Sun have folded and the Houston Comets have been reborn, the only active franchises besides the Dream without a title are the Portland Fire and Toronto Tempo, who joined as expansion clubs in 2026. While the Dream's season ultimately ended in disappointment, there were a ton of positives. The Dream tied a franchise record with 30 wins, finished in the top five in offensive, defensive and net rating, made it out of the first round for the first time since 2018 and made it to the Finals for the first time since 2013. "We've won a lot of great games, and to come all the way to the Finals with this group, I mean, it says a lot," star forward Angel Reese said after Game 7. "And not a lot of people have this opportunity to do it, and like I said, I'd do it all over again with this same group and just battling with them every single day. I love these girls and I love these coaches."
After three consecutive first-round exits, the Dream traded for Reese in the offseason with the hope that she would be the catalyst that turned them into a true title contender. Reese got off to a slow start in Atlanta, and a five-game losing streak in late June and early July -- which included three defeats to the Valkyries -- left the Dream at just 12-9 near the midpoint of the season. And after Reese missed a potential game-winning layup against the Indiana Fever in mid-August, the Dream were stuck in fifth place and in danger of not even getting home-court advantage in the playoffs. That turned out to be an inflection point, however. Reese averaged 19.1 points, 12.3 rebounds, 3.7 assists and 2.3 steals on 56.3% shooting the rest of the way, and the Dream closed the regular season on a 9-1 run to earn the No. 4 seed. Reese continued to excel in the playoffs. With Allisha Gray sidelined for the majority of the semifinals against the New York Liberty, and Rhyne Howard mired in a miserable shooting slump, Reese took over the primary scoring responsibilities to lead the team to the Finals. 
In Game 2 of the Finals, she delivered the best performance of her career: 30 points, 16 rebounds and two blocks to even the series at 1-1 and join Breanna Stewart and Jonquel Jones as the only players in Finals history with a 30-point, 15-rebound game. She followed that up with 21 points, 12 rebounds and three steals in Game 2 to give the Dream a 2-1 lead and join A'ja Wilson as the only players in Finals history with back-to-back 20-point, 10-rebound games. Reese was unable to maintain that level of play against Kiah Stokes and a dogged Valkyries defense, however. She averaged just 9.5 points on 26.7% shooting in the final four games, and had more turnovers (19) than made baskets (12). And she didn't get much help along the way. Gray, still playing through her hand injury, shot 34.1% in the Finals and Howard shot 36%. Reese, who was named Defensive Player of the Year, and earned All-WNBA Second Team honors, made the Dream even better on the defensive end and the glass, and helped them become dominant on the margins. But she didn't solve their biggest issue: shotmaking. This once again doomed them when it mattered most. The Dream shot 33.3% in Game 7, including 6 of 30 from 3-point range. 
"Yeah, it's tough [to process]," Reese said after Game 7. "Especially with the good group, great group, that I've honestly had the honor to battle with all year. They changed my life, and I'm just so grateful for them and I'm so thankful for them. It is tough in the moment, but we'll be back."I always say, delayed, not denied and this is only Year 3," she continued. "They have a lot move years left, too. I'm just really grateful that I got to go to war with this group and I would do it again, all over again."Season at a glanceRecord: 30-14 (No. 4 seed)Offensive rating: 111.9 (4th)Defensive rating: 103.5 (3rd)Net rating: plus-8.4 (3rd)Biggest strength: Winning the marginsWith Reese in the fold, the Dream dominated on the margins. They led the league in offensive rebound rate (35.5%), opponent offensive rebound rate (26.4%) and opponent turnover rate (19.5%). In addition, they were third in free throw rate (0.341) and sixth in turnover rate (16.4%). As a result, they were first in net possessions by a significant margin at +10.4; the Valkyries were second at +6.3. 
Biggest weakness: ShotmakingTrading for Reese did not solve the Dream's biggest issue: shotmaking. Though they were fifth in 3-point rate (.385), they were 12th in 3-point percentage (32.5%) and 33.4% on all jumpshots, which was tied for 13th and the worst mark of any playoff team. Of the team's five players (including DeWanna Bonner, who joined late in the season), that took at least 100 3-point attempts, Howard (35.5%) was the only one to shoot above 35%. Key free agentsDeWanna BonnerBiggest question: Will the Dream make another big move?Since taking over as Atlanta's general manager in 2022, Dan Padover has wheeled and dealed his way to a Finals-level roster. He made five separate trades to acquire all five of the Dream's starters in the Finals -- Howard, Naz Hillmon, Gray, Canada and Reese -- signed Brionna Jones (who missed the playoffs due to a knee injury) and DeWanna Bonner in free agency and drafted Isobel Borlase. After falling short in Game 7, will Padover make another big move? He doesn't have to. The 39-year-old Bonner, who may well retire, is their only notable free agent. Every member of the team's rotation is under contract through 2027, while Gray, Howard, Jones and Hillmon are signed through 2028. 
If Padover believes in this group, the Dream may have the quietest offseason of any team in the league -- especially since they don't have a first-round pick. They could make a few moves on the margins to try and add some depth and shooting, run things back and hope that better injury luck and this season's experience helps put them over the top in 2027. Again, Jones missed the entire postseason and Gray was playing with eight working fingers. But what if Padover believes that they've pushed margin dominance to the limit, or that the team needs more depth? Or, what if he wants to clean up a top-heavy cap sheet that will get even messier now that Reese is eligible for an EPIC (Exceptional Performance on Initial Contract) extension? Padover has never been shy, but all of his big moves to build this roster have been additive, and he's almost exclusively given up picks. We haven't seen him deal a player of significance, as he'd have to this offseason if he wanted to shake up the roster in a meaningful way. 
Jones is the most obvious candidate to be moved. They made it to the Finals largely without her this season, and this was the second time in four seasons that she barely played due to a significant injury. She's also making over $1 million per season through 2028, and getting off that contract would give Padover significantly more flexibility moving forward. A more drastic option would be splitting up the Gray-Howard wing partnership, which has too often failed on the biggest stages, in part due to overlapping skill sets. Gray is on a max deal through 2028, while Howard is making just under the max through the same year. Despite the big contracts and some shaky playoff resumes, both would figure to have significant value. Such a trade does not feel likely, but cannot be ruled out completely given Padover's aggressiveness. WNBA Draft outlookPicks Nos. 27 and 42The Dream traded their 2027 first-round pick to the Sky in the Reese deal, so they won't have a selection until No. 27 overall in the second round. They also have their third-round pick, but that's even less meaningful. It's extremely unlikely that the Dream are going to find anyone with either of their picks who can help them in 2027.

Florida enters the season ranked No. 1 and seeks its second title in three years but will be tested early against in-state foe No. 14 Miami in Tampa.  One of the final games of the night will see a former Pac-12 rivalry renewed when No. 5 Arizona faces No. 22 UCLA in Las Vegas.         Welcome to the Week 8 grades!This might go down as the most bizarre week in NFL history: We saw one team win a game without completing a single pass, we saw a final score that's never happened before and we saw the Ravens lose two quarterbacks to injury before the first half was even over. Here's a closer look at some of the strange things that happened: Baker Mayfield went 0-for-3 passing in the Buccaneers' 16-0 win over the Falcons. That stat line makes the Bucs the first team since 1974 to have zero completions in a win. The Falcons gave up 324 rushing yards to the Bucs, which is the most they've ever surrendered in a game in franchise history. The Ravens became the first team since 2017 to have three different quarterbacks throw a pass in the first half of a game. They lost Lamar Jackson to a thumb injury on the first offensive play and then they ended up losing Tyler Huntley to a toe injury in the second quarter. That left undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano as the only healthy QB on the roster. The Bengals beat the Titans 43-36, giving us a scorigami (that means it was the first time in NFL history that final score has ever happened). The Cowboys blew a two-touchdown lead in the fourth quarter, which had never happened before. The Cowboys were 202-0-1 at home when leading by 14 points or more in the fourth quarter before blowing a 24-10 lead and losing to the Cardinals on Sunday. Jahmyr Gibbs ran through the Vikings with 153 yards on the ground, making him the first player since 2011 to rush for at least 150 yards against a team that went into a game with a record of 6-0 or better. And on Monday night, the Seahawks finally got blown out. The Seahawks had gone 30 straight games without losing a game by five points or more, but that streak ended in a primetime loss to the Bears. It was the fourth-longest streak without a loss of five or more since the AFL-NFL merger in 1970. Speaking of Bears and Seahawks, let's get to the grades, starting with Chicago's big win.

title: Missouri's CJ Gunn ruled ineligble by SEC, Tigers starting C Jaylen Carey indefinitely suspended - CBS Sports
description: Missouri loses a player and suspends another in advance of one of the week's most interesting nonconference match
body:
Missouri loses a player and suspends another in advance of one of the week's most interesting nonconference matchup

    8:19 pm ET

        Missouri guard CJ Gunn has been ruled ineligible by the SEC, Tigers coach Dennis Gates told CBS Sports on Monday. Gates received word from the league office less than two days before Missouri's opening game Tuesday night against Cleveland State.Gunn, whose case was up for dispute for weeks, was banned by the SEC after receiving $524 for playing three games in the Canadian Elite Basketball League in May. By the letter of the SEC's rule, Gunn is ineligible to compete. The SEC passed a rule in the summer that prevented any basketball or football players from returning to play in the SEC if they signed a professional contract after enrolling in college. Gunn, a four-year player, spent his past two seasons at DePaul.
        
            
                United States of College Basketball: Ranking the best team in each state for the 2026-27 season
                
                    Matt Norlander                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
Gunn is ineligible because he signed a pro contract and received less than $600, which Gunn had to pay back, Gates said. The decision came to a head on Monday as Missouri's deadline to formally submit its roster to the SEC loomed Monday evening. No appeal is on the table.
Even worse for Gunn: He's not eligible to be drafted into the G League, which had its draft in October, because the SEC's ruling was finalized too late. The SEC's ruling on Gunn came down to "post-enrollment" status, just as it did with RJ Luis at LSU. Gunn was not expected to be a starter for Missouri but nonetheless would have been a good depth piece on a team with Top 25 aspirations.In holding out Gunn, the SEC stood firm on its stance — and likely did so not just because of its rule, but to reinforce a message to LSU. Although Gunn's situation is notably different from Luis — who left college after 2025 and was trying to play one final season for Will Wade's program — the SEC clearly was not going to allow for any infringement on its new rule. If Gunn were given an exception, LSU would have understandably tried to do the same, potentially bringing yet another lawsuit in the process.
The Gunn news wasn't the only roster hiccup. Projected starting big man Jaylen Carey is indefinitely suspended, Gates told CBS Sports, adding that Carey's violation would not jeopardize his standing with the team. The sit-out is not expected to be long, though it's unclear if Carey will be able to return in time for a highly anticipated game Friday against Saint Louis.

title: NFL reinstates James Pearce Jr. after eight-game suspension: Why EDGE returns at critical time for Falcons - CBS Sports
description: Pearce's insertion into the lineup could be the lift the Falcons need to emerge as the NFC South's top team
body:
Pearce's insertion into the lineup could be the lift the Falcons need to emerge as the NFC South's top team
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    8:09 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        The NFL reinstated Atlanta Falcons edge rusher James Pearce Jr. on Monday, ending the eight-game suspension it handed down before the season began. Pearce will be eligible to play in Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, and coach Kevin Stefanski said last week that the plan is for him to see action in the Week 9 contest. Stefanski said upon Pearce's reinstatement, though, that it is too early to tell how much he will play in his first game back.The Falcons released Jared Ivey and Drake Jackson in corresponding moves with Pearce's activation to the 53-man roster.Pearce's legal troubles early in the 2026 offseason resulted in a violation of the NFL's personal conduct policy, the league ruled. He was arrested on Feb. 7 following a domestic dispute with his then-girlfriend, Rickea Jackson, who stars for the WNBA's Chicago Sky.After his arrest, Pearce faced three felony charges: Aggravated battery with a deadly weapon, fleeing and eluding police and resisting an officer with violence to his or her person. He also faced a felony aggravated stalking charge, but that was later changed to a misdemeanor. A charge of aggravated battery of a law enforcement officer was dropped.
Pearce entered a 12-month pre-trial program, and once it is complete, all the charges will be dismissed. He must also stay out of legal trouble for a six-month period and attend therapy sessions as part of the agreement he and his representation reached in the case.During the legal proceedings, Pearce remained in communication with the Falcons and remained in good enough football shape to potentially be available for Week 9."He's done everything that we've asked him, everything that he's been allowed to do," Stefanski said on Monday. "He's done a great job."
Prolific Falcons pass rush should get even betterExpectations for the Atlanta defensive front heading into the first half of the season were modest given Pearce's suspension and the loss of fellow edge rusher Jalon Walker for the year due to a torn ACL. The second-year players combined for 16 sacks as rookies, and Pearce finished third in Defensive Rookie of the Year voting. Fielding a defense without two young standouts figured to limit the Falcons' ability to pressure the pocket. Instead, they have done more than stay above water in that regard.The Falcons rank seventh in quarterback pressure rate despite blitzing on only 24.1% of snaps. They stand 15th in pass yards allowed per game. That production is, at worst, serviceable for a unit lacking its two projected top pass rushers.Now Pearce arrives poised to potentially take the operation to another level."I don't see it as a challenge," Stefanski said of inserting a new player into the edge rusher rotation. "I see it as a positive to add a good player to the mix. I think the way [Jeff Ulbrich] and the defensive staff have constructed this rush plan, obviously married up with the coverage plan, I think it's beneficial to all parties to do your job. But adding another good player to the mix is a good thing."
Can Pearce aid in stopping the run, too?The Falcons have been solid but not spectacular at defending the run, as they rank 15th in yards allowed per game and eighth in EPA per rush allowed. Last week's performance against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, however, heightened concerns over the defense's ability to contain opposing ball carriers. The defense surrendered a whopping 324 rushing yards to a one-dimensional Buccaneers offense that did not complete a single pass. It did not help that Atlanta could not move the ball, either, but the run-stopping effort played as large of a role in the 16-0 loss as anything.If Pearce levels up as an all-around defender in 2026, he will improve against the run. His greatest impacts come almost exclusively from rushing the passer and stepping back into coverage, so the next step in his development is to threaten ball carriers at or behind the line of scrimmage. The Falcons need that kind of play in order to rebound from their worst showing against the run this year.Pearce's return could impact NFC South racePearce is just one player who will be available for only about half of the season, but his return alone could uplift the Falcons in their hunt for the NFC South title. No team in the division owns more than three wins, and this race is trending toward delivering a sub-.500 champion for the second time in as many years. Since every game matters immensely in such a tight battle, one or two standout performances from Pearce could be the difference between spots in the standings.
NFC South standings1. Panthers (3-4)T-2. Buccaneers (3-5)T-2. Falcons (3-5)4. Saints (2-5)This is a critical time for Pearce to regain eligibility, because the Falcons are about to embark on their toughest four-game stretch yet. On the docket are dates with the Bengals, Kansas City Chiefs, Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions, who are all in play for postseason berths. Even the Cleveland Browns, after that, are more competitive than expected this season, and that contest is on the road.There is no more important time than now for Atlanta's defense to take a step forward, and Pearce can help the unit do so.

        A horde of media quickly engulfed the locker of Steelers defensive back Jaquan Brisker following Pittsburgh's Week 8 win over the Browns. The media was hoping to get Brisker's response to Browns pass rusher Jared Verse's comments leading up to the game, and Brisker obliged in spades. Just a few feet away, Jalen Ramsey — one of the NFL's most well-known and accomplished players — quietly went about his business at his locker. It felt like a good time to ask the eight-time Pro Bowl and three-time All-Pro defensive back about the current state of the Steelers, who enter their Week 9 bye at 6-2 and in sole possession of first place in the AFC North. Ramsey, who turned 32 on Oct. 29, is in the middle of his 11th NFL season and his second season with the Steelers, who acquired him via a trade with the Dolphins in June 2025. During his first nine seasons in the NFL, Ramsey established himself as one of the NFL's premier cornerbacks. In 2021, he won a Super Bowl while being a valued member of the Los Angeles Rams. In his first season with the Steelers, Ramsey was named to his eighth Pro Bowl after filling the stat sheet with 88 tackles, 3.0 sacks, an interception and eight passes defensed while helping Pittsburgh win its first division title since 2020. 
This season, despite dealing with a broken wrist, Ramsey has continued to play at a high level. His signature play through the season's first eight weeks was his sack on the final play of overtime that sealed Pittsburgh's win in Tampa in Week 6. I asked Ramsey about the wrist injury, his one-plus seasons with the Steelers, and Pittsburgh's ascending defense (the Steelers haven't given up a touchdown in seven quarters) and its potential as a championship-caliber unit. I'm sure you're used to playing through injuries at this stage of your career, but a broken wrist is a broken wrist. How are you still able to be such a physical and tenacious player with an injury of that magnitude?   
JR: "God, and a couple pain meds (laughs) and just clearing my mind and going to do it." What still motivates you? I mean, you're a Hall of Famer.JR: "I appreciate that."   What keeps you so passionate and so willing and wanting to play through injuries? And to continue with the tenacity you play with?   JR: "I just think that God has blessed me with a gift and to play football. I don't want to take that for granted any time, no matter the circumstances. And I like playing for my teammates and the fans and the organization. So just that in itself."
You've been on a Super Bowl championship team. I know it's way too premature to put crazy quotes out there...JR: "Yeah, it is. It is." What is, in your opinion, the state of this team now, and maybe even from more of a defensive standpoint, where do you think this team is through eight weeks? JR: "I think we're in a good spot going into the bye week. We've had some highs during the season, but we've had a couple lows as well at different points. And I think that's good to have that type of journey throughout the season at different times, so we can kind of get in our groove, and we can feel kind of the differences at times. So, I think we're in a good spot. That's all I'll say. I don't want to compare anything. I just think we're in a good spot." 
How nice is it to have a running game that runs for 200 yards and kind of keeps you guys off the field like that? JR: "Yeah, I think what our offense is doing right now in terms of their balance, especially our running game, that's a defense's dream. That's all I say. I think anybody on the defensive side would say that."A lot of Steeler fans already kind of look at you as a career Steeler, even though you haven't been here very long. How does it feel to be embraced by the fan base that identifies you as a guy that plays like some of those great Steeler defenders of the past?
JR: "The Steelers have had amazing players in their defenses all throughout the history of this organization — from the front end, the linebackers, the secondary. They've had guys that I've looked up to when I was younger, in high school and college and stuff like that. I kind of model my game after a few people and just their tenacity and the way that they played the game. Their passion, their heart, their physicality, fierceness, and I've tried to play that way my whole career."And obviously, getting traded here last year, it was great to be embraced, knowing that I played the game that way, and that's how they like it around here."

title: Seahawks vs. Bears prediction: Caleb Williams faces toughest test yet in Seattle defense - CBS Sports
description: The Bears take their surging offense into Seattle for a matchup with one of the NFL's best defenses
body:
The Bears take their surging offense into Seattle for a matchup with one of the NFL's best defenses
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:12 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            5 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        In the Week 8 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Seattle Seahawks host the Chicago Bears. Seattle enters this game fresh off a victory over the previously undefeated Kansas City Chiefs, snapping a two-game losing skid. The Seahawks' defense is settling in and once again looks like one of the best units in the league, but faces one of its toughest tests of the season on Monday night.Chicago enters having won both of its games since starting quarterback Caleb Williams returned from injury, improving to 5-2 in the process. The Bears have looked like one of the best offenses in the NFL whenever Williams has been on the field, but they, too, face arguably their toughest test of the season on Monday evening.Will Seattle make it back-to-back wins, or will the Bears ruin their evening with a road upset? How to watch Seahawks vs. Bears liveDate: Monday, Nov. 2 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ETLocation: Lumen Field (Seattle)TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo (try for free)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Seahawks -3, O/U 46.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Bears have the ballChicago has scored, 59, 31 and 30 points in the three Caleb Williams starts that were not played against the Minnesota Vikings in a driving rainstorm. The Bears piled up 552, 368 and 405 yards in those three games, and turned the ball over only twice in those contests.
For the season (including the game against Minnesota), Williams has completed 71% of his passes at an average of 8.2 yards per attempt, both of which are career-high figures. He has thrown five touchdowns against one interception and rushed 24 times for 128 yards and two additional scores. Williams has generally thrown short passes, with an average depth of throw of only 7.0 yards, according to Tru Media. Despite that, he has created explosive passing plays at the third-highest rate in the league (10.7% of dropbacks). That's thanks in large part to the fact that the Bears are averaging 6.4 yards after catch per completion on his throws, the fourth-best mark in the league. The Seahawks, though, limit YAC as well as just about any team in football. They've allowed only 4.5 yards after catch per completion, which ranks third-best in the NFL. They play shell coverages a lot of the time, and they rally to the ball and tackle as well in the secondary as anybody. Their defensive backs and linebackers rarely miss opportunities to bring ball-carriers to the ground. 
The Bears generally want to run the ball more often than almost any team in the league, with a 48.7% rush rate, according to Tru Media. The Seahawks are elite at stopping the run, however, as we saw last week against Kenneth Walker III. D'Andre Swift and Roschon Johnson will have their work cut out for them here, even against a defense that plays a lot of nickel and dime and doesn't load the box.The Chicago offensive line will have to do a lot of work to move Seattle's defensive front off the ball, which has proven extremely difficult for opposing lines this year. When the Seahawks have the ballSeattle's offense is built almost entirely around the exploits of superstar wide receiver Jaxon Smith-Njigba. JSN leads the NFL with 867 receiving yards, 43 receiving first downs and eight receiving touchdowns. He has been targeted on 36.3% of the team's pass attempts, which ranks as the No. 1 mark in the NFL. So does his 33.9% targets-per-route-run rate, which is narrowly ahead of CeeDee Lamb's. 
Smith-Njigba has more receptions than the next three closest players on the Seahawks: AJ Barner, Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed combined for 53. His 867 yards are also considerably more than the 562 that trio has combined as well. They are ancillary pieces at best, and typically they are scarcely involved in the offense. Shaheed is also out on Monday night, which means the secondary options will be even more limited than usual.The Bears, like everyone else in the league, do not have anyone who can cover Smith-Njigba. It's not possible. The best chance to limit him is to get to Sam Darnold and force hurried decisions that lead to turnovers. Darnold, despite missing time due to injury, leads the NFL with eight interceptions. Under pressure, he has been dreadful, completing only 26 of 66 passes for 331 yards, two touchdowns and four picks. He ranks second-to-last in the league in EPA per dropback on pressured plays, per Tru Media. If the Bears can get into his face, they can force him into mistakes and flip the game on its head. 
Something that will help them in that effort is the arrival of defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who is a game wrecker on the interior. Simmons is among the league leaders in both pressures and sacks when lined up inside. He'll have to deal with what is now one of the best guard duos in the league in Quenton Nelson and Grey Zabel, and Simmons could also see his snaps limited in his first game with his new team. (Nelson is likely to play a full complement in his Seattle debut, given how reluctant teams are to rotate offensive linemen.)The Seattle running game should get a boost from the expected returns of Zach Charbonnet and Jadarian Price. Charbonnet hasn't played all season after tearing his ACL during last year's Super Bowl run, while Price has been out since Week 3 with a chest injury. The combination of Emanuel Wilson and George Holani has largely been ineffective, and even if Charbonnet and Price can generate slightly below-average efficiency, they'll represent an improvement over the incumbent duo. The Bears have given up an average of 4.4 yards per carry this season, which ranks 23rd in the league. PredictionSeattle's defense is looking like the unit we expected it to be coming into the year. The Seahawks just shut down Kenneth Walker last week; they should be able to do the same to D'Andre Swift. That puts the entire game on Williams' right shoulder. He can handle that, of course, but it's incredibly difficult to do against Mike Macdonald's unit. That's especially true if the Seahawks get Price and Charbonnet back in the lineup at running back and can run the ball with some degree of success. Pick the Seahawks to take care of business at home. 
Prediction: Seahawks 24, Bears 20

The Seahawks could activate Jadarian Price from injured reserve before Monday night's game, but Mike Macdonald offered few clues about the rookie's status

        Week 8 concludes on Monday night in Seattle, as the Seahawks (4-3) host the Chicago Bears (5-2) at Lumen Field. Running back Zach Charbonnet, who tore his ACL in Seattle's NFC divisional round playoff win against the San Francisco 49ers in January, is primed to make his 2026 season debut. He doesn't have a game status on Seattle's final injury report, indicating he will be available to play. The situation for First-round rookie running back Jadarian Price is slightly murkier.Why the lack of clarity with Price's situation? That is because Price, who has missed the last four games with a chest injury while on injured reserve, would need to be activated by 4 p.m. today. Seattle, however, has already designated Price to return with ESPN among those reporting he will play."We're going to let the transaction speak for itself on that one," coach Mike Macdonald said. 
If the defending Super Bowl champions are going to defeat the high-flying Bears attack led by quarterback Caleb Williams, the Seahawks will need to run the football. Doing so will not only keep Williams on the sideline but also slow down Chicago's pass rush. That second part is key for Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold since he has the NFL's worst expected points added (EPA) per dropback when pressured at -0.63. That's why Seattle traded for Quenton Nelson, and there's a likely chance Nelson will be able to block for both of the Seahawks' top backs in his Seattle debut."We have a plan for Zach and with JD," Macdonald said on Saturday. "If we were to make a move, that would happen on Monday to my knowledge. We'll see if that's what we do. We have some things going on roster-wise that we're working through right now, but we have a plan for Zach."
The Seahawks don't have to activate Price on Monday, but they have two more weeks to make a decision on his status before he would be required to move to season-ending injured reserve. On the off chance Price isn't activated for Week 8, Charbonnet would likely share the rushing workload with Emanuel Wilson. Wilson leads the Seahawks in rushing yards (403), rushing touchdowns (three) and carries (111) .

title: Cardinals name Gardner Minshew as starter, Carson Beck No. 2: What's next for Jacoby Brissett? - CBS Sports
description: Brissett has been demoted to third string after Arizona's comeback win against the Cowboys
body:
Brissett has been demoted to third string after Arizona's comeback win against the Cowboys
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    5:27 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        There have been two surprising developments relating to the Arizona Cardinals' quarterback situation following Sunday's dramatic, come-from-behind win over the Dallas Cowboys. Prior to Sunday's game, Jacoby Brissett was the starter, fellow veteran Gardner Minshew was the backup, and rookie Carson Beck was Arizona's emergency, third-string quarterback. There's a completely new order now.On Monday, head coach Mike LaFleur announced Minshew as the team's new starter. Beck will move to the No. 2 spot while Brissett is now the third-string quarterback. The decision to switch starting quarterbacks was surprising enough; LaFleur's announcement that Brissett, the team's starting quarterback for the majority of the last two seasons, was being demoted to the emergency third spot is the real jaw-dropper. 
Statistically, Brissett wasn't bad during the season's first seven games. But he struggled against the Cowboys before being replaced by Minshew, who caught fire with three touchdown passes while completing 73.9% of his attempts. Minshew's heroics helped turn a 27-17 deficit with 3:54 left into a 33-30 overtime win. The win improved the Cardinals' record to 3-5. 
Minshew, 30, has had a roller coaster NFL career. A 2019 sixth-round pick, Minshew started his career in Jacksonville before having stops in Philadelphia, Indianapolis, Las Vegas and Kansas City prior to coming to Arizona this season. His best season was back in 2023, when he earned his first Pro Bowl nod after going 7-6 as the Colts' starting quarterback. Beck, a 2026 third-round pick, showed potential during this past preseason, going 15-of-19 for 188 yards with a touchdown and no interceptions. His college career included a prolific 2025 season at Miami that ended with an appearance in the College Football Playoff National Championship. 
Minshew will make his debut as the Cardinals' starting quarterback next Sunday in Seattle against the defending Super Bowl champion Seahawks. What's next for Brissett? LaFleur was non-committal when he was asked about Brissett's future with the team beyond this week. That's usually one of the first indicators (another being a demotion) that a player is likely being dealt. The Ravens were the first team to come to mind when the news of Brissett's benching broke. Baltimore desperately needs help at quarterback after losing Lamar Jackson to a possible season-ending injury. Backup Tyler Huntley is also expected to miss some time after injuring his toe during Sunday's loss to the Bills, leaving undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano as the only healthy quarterback on the roster. 
If the Ravens are going to salvage their season, they need to stabilize their quarterback position as best they can. Brissett would help them do that. He could serve as Baltimore's new starting quarterback or at least be a viable backup for Huntley whenever he is cleared to play.On paper, a trade between Baltimore and Arizona for Brissett seems easy. The Ravens need a quarterback, and the Cardinals have one they're not using. It could be as easy as that if both teams agree on the trade terms before the league's Nov. 10 trade deadline. 
        
            
                Should Ravens trade for QB after Lamar Jackson, Tyler Huntley injuries? Possible candidates to watch
                
                    Zachary Pereles                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
The Cardinals need to be realistic here, though. The Ravens need a quarterback, but they're not going to give away too much for a quarterback who just lost his starting job. Baltimore is also probably realistic in terms of its situation. Without Jackson, and playing in a division where every team has a winning record, the odds of the Ravens doing much this season are slim with or without Brissett, who — if nothing else — could help the Ravens remain competitive. 
It would be surprising if the Ravens and Cardinals didn't at least discuss a trade involving Brissett. From the outside, a sixth-round pick sounds fair, or a fifth-round pick in exchange for Brissett and a seventh-round pick. Either way, the Cardinals shouldn't expect to get much in exchange for Brissett, whose time in Arizona has been a disappointment.

title: Should Florida State hire Jimbo Fisher? Weighing pros, cons with ex-Seminoles coach emerging as candidate - CBS Sports
description: A massive Texas A&M buyout means the national championship coach would come cheap, but scheme questions and past
body:
A massive Texas A&M buyout means the national championship coach would come cheap, but scheme questions and past baggage complicate a potential Tallahassee reunion
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 2, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:50 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            4 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        Nearly nine years ago, a 10-foot-tall Christmas tree was spotted in the trash outside of then-Florida State coach Jimbo Fisher's house. Hours later, he accepted the job at Texas A&M, cutting off a successful tenure with the Seminoles. Fisher dominated the ACC after replacing the legendary Bobby Bowden, recording an 83-23 record with three ACC titles and the 2013 national championship. In the years since, the Seminoles have fallen into disarray. It started with Willie Taggart, who was poached to Tallahassee after only a year at Oregon. With primarily Fisher's leftover players, Taggart recorded a miserable 9-12 record before he was fired in his second season. On Sunday, Mike Norvell was fired, setting up the third-highest buyout in the history of college football at $50.3 million. No. 1 on the list? Fisher at Texas A&M ($77.6 million). Now, Fisher has become a rumored candidate to return to Florida State after a hiatus. But after he played a role in Florida State's collapse, would the Seminoles really pull the trigger? 
Pro: He knows Florida StateFisher emerged as one of the most respected college football coaches early in his career. Few coaches have worked for both Bowden and Nick Saban, and Fisher leveraged that know-how and relationships into a monstrous operation at Florida State. If he returned to Tallahassee, he would come with major booster support and financial backing. Fisher would also be able to quickly mend relationships, especially by showing contrition for leaving in the first place. Fisher is also a relentless recruiter and would quickly be able to recreate recruiting inroads in the state of Florida. Will it be enough with Miami and Georgia emerging as recruiting superpowers? That's the big question. 
Con: Fisher might be washedDuring his time at Texas A&M, Fisher emerged as one of the top recruiters in the country. The Aggies signed the No. 1 recruiting class in 2022, the best in history at the time, headlined by eight five-star players. But when it comes to deploying talent, Fisher's tenure was largely a disaster. Fisher's offense is highly dependent on developing quarterbacks, and he continued to struggle in that regard. College football has moved even further away from traditional quarterback development over the years, which could make Fisher's complex offense even more of a liability. Adding insult to injury, Fisher quarterbacks Conner Weigman (Houston) and Haynes King (Georgia Tech) both went on to become exceptional college quarterbacks. They just couldn't produce under Fisher. 
Pro: Fisher would come cheapWhen Texas A&M fired Fisher, they handed him a buyout of more than $70 million. Amazingly, the contract included zero mitigation, meaning that any money that he earns will be on top of the contract. Fisher will receive about $7 million annually from Texas A&M until 2031. Because of the massive income streams, there's no need for Fisher to take on a major salary, like Norvell's $10 million mark. Instead, he could take a low-end ACC salary and put substantially more money into staff and roster, a major necessity as Florida State tries to get back on track. Con: Fisher is stubbornWhen Fisher considered leaving Florida State the first time, his complaints about the state of the program were rising. He wanted more resource and investment, especially from a facilities perspective. 
When he got to Texas A&M, he was handed every resource he could possibly imagine and decided to build everything in his own image. For years, he refused to hire an offensive coordinator at Texas A&M. It only changed when the Aggies stunningly missed a bowl game. Will Fisher be more agreeable in a second trip to Tallahassee, or will his unlimited supply of money to fall back on mean he'll feel insulated from critique? Pro: Fisher winsFor all the complaints about Fisher's shortcomings, he has been a consistent winner. In 14 seasons, Fisher only twice finished below .500. During his final season at Florida State, an interim-coached team still reached a bowl game anyway. Six of his FSU teams finished with 10 wins, and he reached six BCS or CFP bowls. 
Across his career, Fisher has a record of 128-48 with three conference championships. He holds a 75-37 mark in conference games, even finishing 27-21 in SEC play at Texas A&M despite late slippage. Few coaches come with more lines on their resume than Fisher. Con: Can Fisher build an offensive line?There is no greater indicator of program health in the modern era than offensive line play. It's the one position group that really can't be bought in the portal or slapped together; it's a pure developmental group. Late in his tenure at Florida State, Fisher's offensive line groups started to suffer. That atrophy followed into the Taggart and Norvell eras, playing a significant role in the instability of this moment. Fisher's lines at Texas A&M were also inconsistent, especially after losing Josh Henson to USC. 
Now, is Fisher ready to step up and deliver a national-quality offensive line to help develop a competent offense? Norvell failed to do it.The VerdictThere are serious reasons to believe that Fisher could help turn the tide and bring stability back to Florida State. While the Seminoles will lose a big chunk of change to Mike Norvell's buyout, Fisher would help unite the booster community. He also can reassure FSU about many of the shortcomings that ended his first tenure. At the same time, Fisher hasn't put together a productive offense in years. He would be taking over a Florida State that is much more disadvantaged than it was during his heyday. There's no guarantee that the Seminoles could spend at an elite level, especially after paying Norvell's hefty buyout. 
Fisher is worth considering for the administration in Tallahassee, but the drawbacks are hard to ignore.
